newsitem.title: USA: Calif. San Onofre nuclear plants near restart.
newsitem.headline: Calif. San Onofre nuclear plants near restart.

text.p: The 1,070 megawatt (MW) San Onofre 2 nuclear power plant in San Clemente, Calif., is about to return to service following a repair outage, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said Monday.
The NRC, in its daily status report, said the unit was now in hot shutdown, meaning its reactor is still active but not producing power.
The NRC gave the likely restart date as July 16, though SoCal Ed has said it plans to restart the unit July 15.
San Onofre 2 was shut June 29 to replace its charging line check valves.
Meanwhile, the neighboring 1,080 MW San Onofre 3 is also preparing to rejoin the grid. The NRC said the unit is in hot standby and expected to restart July 17.
The unit has been off line since April 12 for a scheduled refueling outage, which was extended to replace the same check valves as were being replaced on unit 2.

The San Onofre generating station is 75 percent owned by SoCal Edison, the principal subsidiary of Edison International, 20 percent by San Diego-based Enova Corp and the rest by two municipal utilities.
